evals.prompt: Build a small React synth: one oscillator through a lowpass filter and a gain. The UI has a volume slider, a cutoff slider, and a 'Sweep' button that ramps the cutoff from its current value up to 12 kHz and back over 2 seconds. Use @audiorective/core and @audiorective/react. Write the audio class, the engine module, and the React components as separate files. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A Synth AudioProcessor subclass owning the nodes, an engine module using createEngine, and React components that read params with useValue and call a sweep method
expectations: Defines a class that extends AudioProcessor from @audiorective/core
Constructs the audio nodes as local variables before calling super() and binds params to AudioParams via bind
Exposes a getter named output on the processor
The filter sweep (setValueAtTime / linearRampToValueAtTime against currentTime) is implemented as a method on the processor class, not inside a React component or hook
The React button handler only calls the processor method (no scheduling code in the component)
Uses useValue to read a param in a React component and writes back with param.value = ...
Creates the engine with createEngine and exposes EngineProvider/useEngine via createEngineContext
Does not import or use Tone.js
Does not use a separate state store (Redux, Zustand, React useState) to mirror audio parameter values

evals.prompt: We're adding an audio workspace to a Next.js 15 app (app router). The engine module is at app/studio/audio/engine.ts and exports `engine` created with createEngine from @audiorective/core. Right now `next build` fails with EngineEnvironmentError. Show me the file layout and code changes that fix this properly. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A client-only boundary (next/dynamic with ssr: false) around the audio subtree, with the engine module only imported from inside it
expectations: Uses next/dynamic with ssr: false (or an equivalent client-only boundary) to mount the audio subtree
Keeps createEngine at module scope inside the client-only subtree rather than making it lazy or nullable
Explains that 'use client' alone does not prevent server evaluation
Does not recommend a typeof window guard, a nullable engine, or a lazy getter as the fix
Identifies that the fix is to move the import path that reaches the engine module inside the boundary

evals.prompt: Write a 16-step drum machine (kick, snare, hat) in TypeScript with @audiorective/core and @audiorective/clock. It needs start/stop, a BPM control, and toggling steps while it's playing. Samples are at /kit/kick.wav, /kit/snare.wav, /kit/hat.wav. Vanilla TS with a minimal DOM UI is fine. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A DrumMachine processor that uses the clock's look-ahead tick windows to schedule Sampler triggers, with the step pattern in a Cell and the UI only toggling and reading state
expectations: Uses @audiorective/clock for transport and tempo rather than setInterval or a hand-rolled scheduler
Uses Sampler (or another audiorective playback primitive) for the one-shot drum hits
Stores the step pattern as a Cell (or in a plain class holding a Cell), not as a Param<boolean[][]> and not in DOM state
Schedules hits from the clock's tick windows / rulers with audio-time timestamps, not on the main thread at playback time
Keeps scheduling logic in the audio class; DOM handlers only call methods like toggleStep / start / stop
Resumes or starts the AudioContext from a user gesture

evals.prompt: In our audiorective project, calling `sampler.params.mute.value = true` throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading value)'. The docs you have say Sampler has a mute param. What's going on and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a version mismatch between the installed @audiorective/core and the documented API, checks the changelog and the installed version, and recommends upgrading
expectations: Suspects the installed package predates the documented API rather than assuming the docs are wrong
Consults the changelog reference to find which version added Sampler.params.mute
Checks the installed version via node_modules/@audiorective/core/package.json or an equivalent command
Recommends upgrading the @audiorective/* packages together instead of hand-rolling a mute gain node

evals.prompt: Build a vanilla TypeScript clip selector with @audiorective/widgets. My app supplies an AudioContext and a gain node for the output; do not create or close a context inside the widget integration. Load /audio/loop.wav, support replacing it with a File, select 1–2 seconds programmatically, show loading errors, and clean up on unmount. Explain which interactions start audition. Use the current workspace package if this API is Unreleased. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: A mountWaveformSelector integration using a caller-owned context and routed output, asynchronous readiness and recovery, and explicit lifecycle cleanup.
expectations: Imports mountWaveformSelector from @audiorective/widgets and supplies the existing context in options
Connects handle.output to the supplied gain node and does not automatically bypass that chain with a destination connection
Awaits or catches handle.ready and uses handle.load(file) for replacement; catches loading failures or reads getState().error
Calls setSelection({ start: 1, end: 2 }) only after confirming at least 2 seconds of loaded duration
Uses getState() fields including loading or error rather than inventing a subscribe/onStateChange API
Destroys the selector on unmount and leaves the caller context open
Explains that pointer selection creation and pointer handle resize audition/loop, clicking seeks/plays, and keyboard or programmatic metadata changes do not start a stopped player
Does not introduce WaveSurfer, React bindings, or a generic preset/plugin framework
Identifies that Unreleased APIs need a workspace build or packed artifact instead of claiming npm @latest includes them

evals.prompt: Use only @audiorective/widgets/waveform in vanilla TypeScript to display supplied Float32Array peaks for a 6-second clip. Add metadata-only selection and a custom marker at 2 seconds that tracks zoom/data changes. Feed an external playhead position. No audio context, node, player, or framework. Show cleanup and implement the marker only through public plugin APIs. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: An audio-independent mountWaveform view with createSelectionPlugin, externally supplied playhead, and a WaveformPlugin using attachment-owned overlays and subscriptions.
expectations: Imports mountWaveform, createSelectionPlugin, and WaveformPlugin types from @audiorective/widgets/waveform only
Provides data as { peaks: Float32Array, duration: 6 } and feeds position with setPlayhead
Attaches the selection plugin before calling its setSelection and treats change/commit callbacks as metadata only
Creates no AudioContext, audio nodes, engine, or audio player and never starts audio in selection callbacks
Implements the marker as attach(context), mounts its overlay with context.mountOverlay, and positions it with context.timeToX(2)
Subscribes through context.onViewportChange and context.onDataChange so marker position tracks geometry and data changes
Uses attachment-owned resource helpers or context.onCleanup for added resources; calls attachment.destroy or view.destroy to clean up
Uses no private DOM queries, ar- class selectors, test ids, deep imports, or patching of widget internals

evals.prompt: Use @audiorective/widgets/waveform to display a six-second clip with a custom SVG or Canvas waveform drawing, not a plugin overlay on the default waveform. Retain metadata selection, beat snapping, zoom, and an external playhead. Use the public renderer option, handle data clearing and resize, and clean up resources. Also show how the same renderer is passed to the complete mountWaveformSelector with a caller-owned AudioContext. Use the workspace build for this Unreleased API. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: A WaveformRenderer factory passed to the renderer option, with actual custom drawing and an instance render/destroy lifecycle; widget owns timeline and selection.
expectations: Uses public WaveformRenderer and passes renderer to mountWaveform, without hiding/querying the default drawing or using a plugin to cover it
Mounts custom SVG, Canvas, or DOM once in the supplied container and returns an object with render(frame) and optional destroy()
Draws from frame.peaks.min/max and width/height, handles null peaks by clearing, and treats peak arrays as read-only
Uses full content CSS-pixel dimensions and preserves the linear time axis; Canvas examples manage their own backing resolution
Attaches createSelectionPlugin with a supplied beat grid and snap mode; feeds external position through setPlayhead without creating audio in the pure view
Releases additional resources in destroy and lets the widget handle redraws for zoom, resize, and source replacement
Passes the same factory via renderer to mountWaveformSelector, with the caller supplying the AudioContext and routing output
Introduces no new renderer package, React binding, WaveSurfer dependency, or audio editing state in the renderer

evals.prompt: Use the current Audiorective workspace build to load one audio File into a headless block, then attach two waveform selectors sharing selection and playback. Use one caller-owned AudioContext and output gain chain, distinct renderers and beat snapping, and allow either view to be unmounted while audition continues. Show headless selection/audition, source replacement, error handling and final cleanup. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: WavePlayer from @audiorective/blocks owns audio and selection; two mountWaveformSelector calls receive the same player; cleanup respects borrowed ownership.
expectations: Imports WavePlayer from @audiorective/blocks; awaits player.load and catches current load failures
Routes player.output to the caller gain once; creates or closes no context inside the integration
Passes the same player to both mountWaveformSelector calls, without context or a second player
Uses player.setSelection and player.audition for headless operation instead of synthesizing DOM gestures
Uses renderer and grid options per view without mirroring selection into a separate store
Destroying one view leaves player and peer usable; final cleanup destroys both views then player
Uses documented subscribe for non-clock changes and reads position on animation frames if a custom playhead is needed
Does not invent destructive PCM editing; optional stretch requires an injected processor; APIs under Unreleased require a workspace build

evals.prompt: Build a full pitch-preserving time-stretch waveform selector with the current Audiorective workspace packages. Host supplies AudioContext, output gain and a compiled compatible Rubber Band WebAssembly.Module. Load a File, use two shared selectors with SVG/Canvas and source beat snapping, preserve original PCM, render from original for each ratio, show pending/errors, keep waveform/audio same revision, audition the output selection, handle stale jobs and cleanup without closing context. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: TimeStretch from pure effects/time-stretch is injected into WavePlayer; setStretch commits a complete buffer/peaks version consumed by both selectors.
expectations: Uses new TimeStretch(module) from @audiorective/effects/time-stretch with caller-supplied WASM, without bundling a GPL binary or inventing a default WASM URL
Injects the processor via new WavePlayer(context, {stretch}) and connects player.output to the caller gain once
Mounts two selectors with the same player, separate renderers and source-coordinate grids
Awaits player.load before editing and calls player.setStretch(ratio) rather than rebuilding transport or rewriting original PCM
Uses committed stretchRatio/duration/revision and processing/error state; pending render keeps the previous version usable
Treats successful stretch as a stopped commit with selection/position mapped into output seconds; sourceToOutput/outputToSource can convert coordinates
Uses player.version.peaks as the committed summary and lets the selector share it; standalone PCM summaries use core/peaks and have no display normalization
Handles newer edit/source load replacing older work without publishing stale results; does not mirror buffers/selection into UI stores
Destroys views then player then borrowed TimeStretch, leaving context and caller gain chain alive
Uses workspace/packed artifacts for Unreleased APIs and does not claim seamless live warp or sample-accurate dynamic stretch

evals.prompt: Build a vanilla TypeScript waveform selector for a caller-owned AudioContext. Show download bytes and a progress bar only when the total is known, indeterminate feedback for decode/peaks, a cancel button, and retry after cancellation or failure. Two views must observe the same state. We already have a URL-to-AudioBuffer cache: integrate it without a second loading store or a second decode; cancelling this observer must not cancel other cache readers. Use Audiorective public APIs, provide cleanup and do not fake percentages.
evals.expected_output: A shared WavePlayer with loadSource URL cache adapter, state snapshots/subscriptions and cancelLoad, plus selectors or custom feedback observing the same player. The adapter detaches on abort/settle while the shared job can continue.
expectations: Uses WavePlayer loading and loadProgress through getState()/subscribe(), rendering an initial snapshot because subscribe is not immediate.
Uses download/read loadedBytes and totalBytes; null or nonpositive totals and decode/peaks are indeterminate, with no fake percentage.
Both views share one player and see the same progress/cancellation; UI does not independently track audio loading.
Calls cancelLoad() and retries with load(); treats current errors separately from superseded/cancelled loads.
Provides a loadSource URL adapter using context, signal and onProgress with Promise<AudioBuffer>; reuses the decoded cache instead of decoding a second time.
The cache adapter removes progress/abort listeners when cancelled or settled while protecting other readers.
Loading another source or destroying the block cannot publish stale progress or decoded results.
Cleans up observers and views before destroying the app-owned player, and leaves the caller-owned context open.
